meta.ground_truth_method: manual source inspection of The Undiscovered Self PDF and chunk artifacts; never derived from the retriever under test

items.question: mass-mindedness
items.notes: Defining section opening (c00035) and core passages on the stultification/moral irresponsibility of mass-mindedness.

items.question: self-knowledge
items.notes: Section-defining passages: people measure self-knowledge by the average person (c00011/12); rigorous self-examination (c00166); meaning of self-knowledge (c00201).

items.question: What does Jung mean by a 'metamorphosis of the gods'?
items.reference_answer: A transformation of fundamental principles and symbols, expression of the changing unconscious man within us.
items.notes: c00208 contains the only explicit 'metamorphosis of the gods' passage: change of fundamental principles and symbols driven by the unconscious man within us.

items.question: yucca moth
items.notes: Illustrative symbiosis example; both chunks carry the example.

items.question: What split is symbolized by the 'Iron Curtain'?
items.notes: c00005 raises the symbolic split (p11); c00121 states the barbed-wire line runs through the psyche of modern man (p55).

items.question: Why does the individual lose independence in a mass society?
items.notes: Individual becomes an abstract number / statistical nullity (c00029, c00032); de-individualized society succumbs to the dictator - a million zeros add up to nothing (c00100); crowd size makes the individual negligible (c00030).

items.question: What protects an individual from being absorbed into the psychology of the mass?
items.notes: Religious standpoint enables judgment (c00036); individual relation to God as shield (c00103); resistance through individuality as organized as the mass (c00111); certainty keeping one from dissolving in the crowd (c00164).

items.question: How does Jung describe the fear of the unconscious psyche?
items.notes: Fear impedes self-knowledge and is the gravest obstacle to psychology (c00088); natural cowardice of most men (c00098).

items.question: Why is statistical science a problem for understanding the individual?
items.notes: Statistical theories abolish exceptions (c00012); average-unit anthropology removes paramount individual features (c00017); individual judged a repeating unit (c00020); statistical-only reality makes judgment impossible (c00036).

items.question: What happens when people band together into groups and organizations?
items.notes: Banding together extinguishes individual personality and makes society succumb to a dictator; a million zeros do not add up to one.

items.question: What did Jung observe about propaganda in Eastern Europe?
items.notes: Communal propaganda's superficial effect shown by recent events in Eastern Europe; footnote added January 1957.

items.question: According to Jung, how do the Churches use mass action?
items.notes: Churches avail themselves of mass action to cast out the devil with Beelzebub despite caring for the individual soul.

items.question: What does Jung call a two-edged weapon and why?
items.notes: '[An] indispensable aid in the organization of masses and is therefore a two-edged weapon' (c00056; value of community depends on the spiritual and moral stature of individuals).

items.question: What does recognition of the shadow lead to?
items.reference_answer: Modesty to acknowledge imperfection; basis of human relationships.
items.notes: Leads to the modesty needed to acknowledge imperfection, the ground of real human relationships.

items.question: Why does Jung think people project evil onto others?
items.notes: We prefer to localize evil in individual criminals while washing our hands of it (c00184); the blacker-painted human shadow (c00178).

items.question: What does Jung say about nuclear weapons and moral responsibility?
items.notes: Reason alone does not suffice against hellish experiments; fear of the evil in one's own bosom checks reason; deciding factor lies with the individual man.

items.question: How does Jung describe the State taking the place of God?
items.notes: The dictator State swallows religious forces; State has taken the place of God; policy exalted to creed, leader becomes a demigod beyond good and evil.

items.question: What is Jung's criticism of laboratory psychology?
items.notes: It proceeds abstractly, removing itself from its object, so its findings are remarkably unenlightening for practical purposes.

items.question: In what sense does Jung call the psyche a cosmic principle?
items.notes: Consciousness is a precondition of being, giving the psyche the dignity of a cosmic principle coequal with physical existence.

items.question: What argument about immortality does Jung attribute to the crowd?
items.notes: 'They have the most convincing reason for not believing in immortality: all those people want to be immortal!' - bigger crowd, more negligible the individual.

items.question: In the chapter on the West, why does Jung think Western Europe may be immune to mass seduction?
items.notes: Western Europe forms the real political backbone, immune because of the outspoken counterposition of the Christian churches.

items.question: What does Jung say has happened to 'the Word' in Western thought?
items.notes: The word has literally become our god; universal validity severs its original link with the psyche.

items.question: What happens when instinct is violated or neglected?
items.notes: Painful physiological and psychological consequences requiring medical help; unconscious exists as counterbalance to consciousness.

items.question: What role does Jung give to modern art and the unconscious Zeitgeist?
items.notes: Modern art performs psychological education by breaking down previous aesthetic views; the Zeitgeist compensates the conscious attitude and anticipates change.

items.question: Does Jung say Christ ever called his disciples at a mass meeting?
items.notes: Rhetorical question pair spanning the page boundary: c00103 raises it, c00104 continues with the feeding of the five thousand.

items.question: Besides huge agglomerations of people, what chief factor does Jung name for psychological mass formation?
items.notes: The passage spans the page boundary: c00028 introduces the chief factor, continuing over c00029 (loss of foundations/dignity).

items.question: On what foundation do freedom and autonomy of the individual rest?
items.notes: Not ethical principles or creeds but relation to an extramundane authority acting as counterpoise to the world (spans p24-25).

items.question: What advantage does the religious person have for answering crucial questions?
items.notes: Enjoys a great advantage: immediate experience supplies facts where others must rely on proofs.

items.question: What does Jung predict history will do to those who resist the inevitable development?
items.notes: History will pass over those who feel vocationally bound to resist; still necessary to cling to what is essential and good in tradition.

items.question: What Greek concept does Jung use for 'the right time'?
items.notes: Kairos - we are living in what the Greeks called the Kairos, the right time for a metamorphosis of the gods.
